convertibility_reason: Uses custom indicators XFatl and XSatl via iCustom calls which are non-standard indicators requiring external .mqh/indicator files. Trading logic depends on cloud coloring from these custom indicators, making it impossible to auto-convert without reimplementing the custom indicator logic.

derived_values.name: Cloud direction from XFatl/XSatl indicator buffer colors

other_exits: Closes opposite position on signal reversal when position_gate is no_opposite_side

position_sizing.conditional_logic: negative input=fixed lots, positive input=risk percentage of deposit

custom_logic_notes: EA uses two custom indicators XFatl and XSatl to form a cloud. The cloud color (determined by the relationship between the two indicator lines) determines the trading direction. When the cloud turns bullish (XFatl above XSatl), a long position is opened; when bearish, a short position is opened. The opposite position is closed first before opening a new one. Signal is evaluated on bar close using previous bar values (shift=1) to avoid repainting. Position sizing has dual mode: negative input values are treated as fixed lot size, positive values as risk percentage of free margin.
external_dependencies: CSignalXFatlXSatlCloud.mqh (possible signal module from Standard Library)
python_conversion_notes: The custom indicators XFatl and XSatl must be fully reimplemented in Python before the trading logic can be converted. The cloud logic requires understanding the internal calculation of both indicators. Without the indicator source code, one would need to reverse-engineer the indicator algorithms or export their values from MT5 for use in Python. The ATR-based SL/TP is straightforward. The dual-mode position sizing (negative=fixed lots, positive=risk percent) requires explicit branching logic. New bar detection pattern should use pandas resample or timestamp comparison. The signal uses previous bar values (shift=1) which is important for preventing look-ahead bias in Python backtests.
